report.title: Five detained in Água Clara with about 54.5 kg of marijuana
report.summary: Military and Civil Police in Água Clara detained five men on 4 November 2026 after a tip about drug sales from a white Volkswagen Gol, and seized 59 marijuana tablets weighing about 54 kg plus another 500 g. Four were arrested in flagrante for trafficking and one was taken on an existing warrant; cocaine from the same searches is not counted as cannabis.

open_questions: The cannabis figure is the 59 tablets of about 54 kilograms plus the separately stated 500 grams; a few further home portions of marijuana had no weight, and the combined 54.64 kilogram total includes cocaine so it is not used.
Cocaine found in the car and in a discarded bag, about 120 grams in 19 portions, is not counted as cannabis.

Portal Água Clara says the other two people were found at a snack bar and the tablets were found afterwards, while the Civil Police account says the tablets and the two men were at a second address used as a store.
The submitted account places a drug hide in woodland near the MS-324, but neither article body locates the 59 tablets there.
No court hearing or sentence was reported; four men were arrested in flagrante and one was taken on an existing warrant.
The material was described as marijuana or a substance resembling it, with no laboratory confirmation reported.
Coordinates are for the town of Água Clara, not a point in Jardim das Palmeiras.
report.body:
Military Police in Água Clara, Mato Grosso do Sul, stopped a man on Wednesday 4
November 2026 after an anonymous tip that he was selling drugs from a white
Volkswagen Gol in the Jardim das Palmeiras neighbourhood. The driver tried
to flee when he saw the police car, was chased for several blocks and was
stopped. In the car officers found a portion of a substance resembling
cocaine, and at the suspect's home they seized portions of marijuana, a
precision scale, packaging material and cash. The police action began on
the night of Wednesday 4 November after an anonymous tip that a vehicle was
being used to sell drugs in the town. Officers then went to the 30-year-old
driver's home, where they found further portions of marijuana and a precision
scale. The suspect was already a target of the Civil Police General
Investigations Section.

A joint Military Police and Civil Police team then found two more people at a
snack bar, and later found 59 tablets of a substance resembling marijuana
weighing about 54 kilograms. The Civil Police said the 59 marijuana
tablets, weighing about 54 kilograms, were found at a second address used as a
store, and that two men aged 18 and 20 were arrested in flagrante there.
Investigators then stopped a 22-year-old with about 500 grams of marijuana and a
precision scale. They also found a bag with 19 portions of cocaine
totalling about 120 grams, which the Civil Police said the first suspect had
discarded during the Military Police stop. A fifth man, aged 28, was found
and arrested on an outstanding warrant; he was already under investigation for
drug trafficking.

The operation's tally was about 54 kilograms and 640 grams of marijuana and
cocaine together, plus a car, a motorcycle, three precision scales, three mobile
phones, packaging and about R$250 in cash. Five men were detained in all:
four were arrested in flagrante for drug trafficking and association for
trafficking, and the fifth was taken on the existing warrant. The people
involved were taken to the Civil Police station in Água Clara.

report.body:
João Victor Castro was arrested after being caught with substances analogous to
marijuana and cocaine on the afternoon of Thursday 12 November 2026. The
stop took place at about 17:45 at Travessa São Sebastião with Rua Joana D'Arc in
Mojuí dos Campos. Soldiers of the 35th Military Police Battalion said he
was with his wife, who, when questioned, said there was more illicit material at
the couple's home. The officers went to the address on Rua Almirante
Barroso in the Cidade Alta 2 neighbourhood.

At the house the Military Police found R$301 in cash, 31 wraps of a substance
analogous to cocaine and 12 wraps of a substance analogous to marijuana.
They also found a portion of drug set aside outside the packages, several
packages used to hold drugs, and a black Samsung A14 mobile phone. The
material presented also included one greenish portion resembling marijuana.

After the flagrant offence, the suspect and the seized material were taken for
the applicable procedures at the 16th Civil Police Section in Santarém.
João Victor remained at the disposal of the courts.

report.body:
The New Cairo Criminal Court, sitting in the Fifth Settlement, sentenced a woman
described as a worker to six years of aggravated imprisonment for possessing
hashish for trafficking in the Badr police district.

The referral order said she held hashish for trafficking, without legal
authorisation, on 22 April 2026 in the Badr police district. A deputy
investigations officer of the Badr police station, posted at a security
checkpoint in the district, said she looked suspicious, asked to search her
belongings and, with her consent, found 125 brown pieces of hashish, a sum of
money and a mobile phone.

According to the officer's account, she admitted holding the drugs for
trafficking, said the money came from that activity and said the phone was used
to contact customers. A chemical laboratory report said 30 samples from the
125 pieces, which together weighed 9 kilograms and 350 grams, tested as hashish
listed in the schedules of the anti-drug law.

open_questions: Actu.fr rounds the seizure to 33 kilograms in its headline and lead, while its own body and the other two accounts give 32.8 kilograms, which is the figure used.

Actu.fr gives the fine as 132,000 euros, described as the value of the goods, while La Semaine des Pyrénées itemises customs fines of 131,200 euros and 405 euros, totalling 131,605 euros; the itemised total is used.
Actu.fr says the Tarbes court tried the driver for tobacco trafficking and laundering the proceeds of fraud, which does not match the cannabis facts the same article and the other accounts report.
Only the Tarbes Infos account reports the remand warrant, the Telegram recruitment, the 3,000 euro payment and the Alicante to Poland route.
The French customs administration's own statement could not be found, so the account rests on three local outlets, one of which quotes a customs communiqué.
The driver is not named in any of the accounts, and no appeal or later court step is reported.
report.body:
On the evening of 28 September 2026, customs officers stopped a Ukrainian driver
at Saint-Lary-Soulan, in the Hautes-Pyrénées, and found more than 32 kilograms
of cannabis herb in the vehicle he was driving. Customs said the seizure,
made that evening, came to 32.8 kilograms of cannabis herb. The Cierp-Gaud
customs brigade, based in Haute-Garonne, carried out the stop in the middle of
the night as the driver came from Spain in a car registered in Poland.

Officers found the cannabis in 32 bags, weighing 32.8 kilograms in all, hidden
in two compartments built under the front seats. A customs statement said
the Polish registration and the driver's vague answers led officers to look
closer, and that an unusual thickness in the floor hid the two compartments. The driver, a Ukrainian living in Poland with no criminal record, said he
had been recruited through Telegram to carry the goods from Alicante to Poland
for 3,000 euros. Investigators said the route used the Aragnouet-Bielsa
tunnel, and officers also seized 405 euros in cash after the driver tried to
mask the smell with white spirit.

He was tried on 1 October 2026 by the criminal court in Tarbes, which sentenced
him to 24 months in prison and banned him from French territory for ten years. The court also imposed a customs fine of 131,200 euros for transporting
narcotics without proper documents, plus a customs fine of 405 euros for customs
money laundering, 131,605 euros in customs fines in all. The 32.8 kilograms
of cannabis herb were confiscated, together with 405 euros in 50, 20 and 5 euro
notes, two telephones and a computer. He was tried at an immediate hearing
and the two-year prison term was ordered with a remand warrant, the Tarbes Infos
account said.
